_comment: Copyleft-source manifest for binary releases (LGPL-2.x / MPL).
Each entry maps a DLL name pattern (glob, matched against the
release_manifest.json of a built installer staging) to the exact
upstream source archive that corresponds to the shipped binary.
Before every binary release: fill version / source_url / sha256 for
every entry that matches a shipped DLL, then run
scripts/release/collect_lgpl_sources.py -- it fails closed on any
matched DLL whose source pin is incomplete.
The pin has to identify the build that actually ships. NOTICE already
tells the user they can obtain the sources; pointing only at the
upstream project does not identify which version that is, which is
cls-studio uses no video I/O at all, but opencv-python-headless bundles
FFmpeg regardless. The Windows wheel carries OpenCV's own LGPL-2.1+
macOS wheel carries a GPL build instead, which is why no macOS bundle

provenance: whose ffmpeg/download_src.sh builds the shipped DLL from FFmpeg tag n4.4.5.
Cross-checked against ffmpeg_version.cmake in the same commit:
The same DLL statically links openh264 (BSD-2) and libvpx (BSD-3);
neither is copyleft, so neither carries a source-offer obligation.
